$comment: Spec §6: 'Agenda coordinates are derived, not invented.' This file IS the derivation.
The ingest spike (see docs/INGEST-SPIKE.md) found that the Shallow Review 2025 pipeline
publishes a machine-readable `orthodox_problems` field on 59/79 agendas — this is the
'stated assumptions' field §6 depends on, and it draws from a CLOSED VOCABULARY of only
12 canonical problems (Yudkowsky's AGI Ruin list). That collapses the §6 workload from
62 agendas x 17 axes = 1054 hand judgements down to 12 problems x 17 axes, plus 8 family
priors, plus two small enum maps. Every number below is a claim about what an assumption
IMPLIES about a belief axis, and each carries a `why` string that renders in-product next
Precedence when composing an agenda coordinate (see scripts/lib/derive.ts):
Contributions are combined as a weighted mean, then clamped to [-1, 1]. An axis that
receives NO contribution stays null. Null is a first-class value (spec §7) — never impute.

orthodox_problems.$comment: Closed vocabulary. NOTE for the parser: two entries contain literal commas ('...steganography, spearphishing' and 'Fair, sane pivotal processes'), so the field CANNOT be naively comma-split. scripts/lib/parse-orthodox.ts tokenizes against this vocabulary longest-first.

Value is fragile and hard to specify.why: If the target is hard to state, the failure is a knowledge failure rather than a will failure, and getting values right is not the same problem as avoiding catastrophe.

Corrigibility is anti-natural.why: If shutdown-acceptance cuts against the grain of competent optimization, it cannot be bolted onto a system after the fact — which is an argument both against containment and for redesign.

Goals misgeneralize out of distribution.why: The central misalignment claim. Note it argues for misalignment WITHOUT arguing for concealment: a misgeneralizing system is not thereby a deceptive one, so this pushes p_scheme very slightly down.

Instrumental convergence.why: Convergent self-preservation and resource acquisition give a misaligned system a reason to hide and to resist correction.

Superintelligence can fool human supervi.why: This is the direct argument that behavioural testing is not assurance — the strongest single derivation available for the internals axis.

Superintelligence can hack software supe.why: If the supervisor is itself a system that can be subverted, automated oversight inherits the problem it was meant to solve.

A boxed AGI might exfiltrate itself by s.why: A claim specifically about the failure of physical and informational boxing, which is the containment axis in its purest form.

Humanlike minds/goals are not necessaril.why: Undercuts the 'train it to be a decent person' family of approaches — human-likeness is not a safety property.

Humans cannot be first-class parties to.why: A bargaining-position claim: surviving is not the same as retaining influence, so a good long-run outcome has to be actively secured.

Someone else will deploy unsafe superint.why: A race claim. The binding constraint becomes coordination rather than knowledge, and the locus of risk moves to competition between actors.

Fair, sane pivotal processes.why: Shorthand in the source for 'fair, sane pivotal processes are unavailable' — a claim that the coordination route is closed, so will rather than knowledge is binding.

Pivotal processes require dangerous capa.why: If the fix requires building the dangerous thing, the risk shifts toward deliberate use of capability rather than unintended behaviour.

families.$comment: Spec §6: 'Score at the family level first, let agendas inherit, then override only where an agenda is atypical.' Keys are the `section` values in the Shallow Review agendas export — all 8 are present and exhaustive.

Black-box safety (understand and control.why: Defined by the source as shaping behaviour through input-output optimization 'without requiring deep understanding of internal mechanisms' — the low pole of internals by definition, and a commitment to working on the systems that exist.

White-box safety (i.e. Interpretability).why: The internals axis is this family's defining commitment.

Evals.why: Measurement of deployed behaviour. Presumes that catching a problem in testing is possible and useful, which is a containment-feasible position; leans behavioural by construction.

Theory.why: Substrate-independent understanding aimed at architectures not yet built. Implies both that current systems are the wrong object of study and that there is time to do foundational work.

Safety by construction.why: The name is the position: guarantees come from how the system is built, not from patching how it behaves.

Make AI solve it.why: The automation axis is this family's defining bet, and it only pays off if capable systems arrive while the problem is still open.

Multi-agent first.why: Locates risk in interaction between many actors and systems rather than in a single system's goals — closer to structural and power-distribution failure than to a lone misgeneralizing agent.

Labs (giant companies).why: Revealed position of an organization that is building the systems and doing safety work on them in-house.

target_case.$comment: Maps the source's `target_case_text` enum. Spec §8 stores this on the agenda as `target_case`. It is a statement about which world the agenda is trying to be useful in, which is a direct read on the misalignment-chain axes.

worst-case.why: Designed to hold up against a system that is misaligned and actively adversarial.

pessimistic.why: Assumes things go badly but not adversarially.

average.why: Targets the modal world, which presumes failures are the ordinary kind and are catchable.

mixed.why: No signal — the source declines to commit.

varies.why: No signal — the source declines to commit.

broad_approach.$comment: Maps `broad_approach_text`. Values in the source are compound ('engineering / cognitive'), so the parser splits on '/' and averages the matched components. 'behavioural' and 'behavioral' both occur — normalize spelling before lookup.

behavioral.why: Studies input-output behaviour. Weak pull: the source's behaviourist/cognitivist split is about whether the agenda models the system as having internal cognition, which is upstream of, but not the same as, our internals axis (does ASSURANCE require opening the model up). Treated as a proxy, not a reading.

cognitive.why: Treats the system as having internal cognition worth modelling. Weak pull, for the reason given under `behavioral`: the source labels Debate 'cognitive' though debate never opens the weights, so this field over-reads if taken at full strength.

engineering.why: Builds artefacts rather than characterizing them; weakly favours working with what exists.

maths / philosophy.why: Foundational work aimed at systems not yet built.

composition.$comment_weights: Orthodox problems outweigh family priors because they are what the agenda's own proponents wrote down, which is the whole point of §6. target_case slightly outweighs family because it is stated per-agenda rather than inherited. EXCEPTION: on a family's `authoritative` axes the family prior carries `family_authoritative` weight instead. Calibration found the reason — an agenda that lists 'Superintelligence can fool human supervisors' is often naming the problem its method ATTACKS, not asserting that assurance therefore requires interpretability. Debate cites it and is squarely behavioural. Without this exception the derivation flipped Debate to internals-positive. The family prior still only outweighs, never overrides: magnitude stays responsive to the assumptions.
composition.$comment_null: An axis with zero contributions stays null and drops out of that agenda's distance calculation, symmetrically with a user abstention (spec §7).

not_derivable.$comment: Axes no Shallow Review field speaks to. These stay null on every technical agenda unless the owner assigns them, and the UI must show them as unknown rather than centred. This list is the single largest driver of OWNER-DATA item OD-03.
not_derivable.note: The three policy axes being null on technical agendas is CORRECT — domain gating (spec §5) means technical targets are never scored on them. `patienthood` is the real gap: it is a core-scope axis, so it enters every match, and nothing in the source speaks to it.
